• The rules for changing Direct Speech to Indirect Speech:

• Use that in the sentence of indirect speech.

 * Shakespeare said that he would write another drama the next day.* (Indirect speech)
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Example: * **She said to me, “Where did you buy this dress from?” *(Direct speech)

 * **She asked me where I had bought that dress from. *(Indirect speech)

• Commas और inverted commas हटा दे।
 
• Reported speech में first person, reporting speech के subject के अनुसार बदलता है।
 
• Indirect speech के वाक्य में that का प्रयोग करें।
 
 
• Example: *Shakespeare said, “I will write another drama tomorrow.” *(Direct speech)

 __

 ​

__
 
• Steps for solving Para Jumbles:
 
 
• Clues include pronouns, like he, she, it, this, that, these, those; adverbs like formally, really; article a, an and the; definers like actually, finally, another; connectors like but, yet, both, also and neither nor, or, however, nevertheless.
 
• Now, with the help of clues, try to find out qualifier and qualified sentences, so that we can make pairs of qualified and qualifier sentences to eliminate the wrong choices given in the question.

• Opener, D होगा क्योंकि यह पैराग्राफ के संदर्भ का परिचय देता है।
 
• इसके बाद, A आएगा क्योंकि यह रणजी के स्कूल के बारे में जानकारी जोड़ता है।

questions.question: A person saves 25% of his income. If his income increases by 20% and his saving remains the same, then what will be the increased percentage of his expenditure?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let initial Income = 100, which means Savings = 25 and Expenditure = 75.

New Income = 120 (increased by 20%) and Savings = 25 (remains constant).

New Expenditure = 120 − 25 = 95.

Increase in Expenditure = 95 − 75 = 20.

Percentage Increase = (20 ÷ 75) × 100 = 26 ²/₃%.

**∴ The correct answer is 26 ²/₃%.**

A person saves 25% of his income.

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Increase = (Increase in Value ÷ Original Value) × 100

 
 Initial Income = 100

Income-Expenditure Concept

The foundational equation is **Income = Expenditure + Savings**. Any change in income will exactly equal the sum of changes in expenditure and savings.

Constant Variable Effect

Loss % = (150 − 120) ÷ 150 × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is Loss 20%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price at 1st condition = 33⅓% of original selling price

Loss at 1st condition = 33⅓%

Selling price at 2nd condition = 40% of original selling price

**Formula Used:**

Loss = Cost Price (CP) − Selling Price (SP)

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/470330812c4ab463d852d392ccec453d2521143f39a9d4653feb4883e0783217.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Original Selling Price = SP and Cost Price = CP

⇒ Selling price in 1st condition = 33⅓% of SP = SP ÷ 3

⇒ Loss % in 1st condition = 33⅓% = 1/3

⇒ SP ÷ 3 = CP − (1/3 × CP)

⇒ SP ÷ 3 = 2/3 × CP

⇒ SP = 2 × CP

⇒ Selling Price in 2nd condition = 40% of SP = 0.4 × (2 × CP) = 0.8 × CP

⇒ Since New SP is less than CP, there is a loss.

⇒ Loss = CP − 0.8 × CP = 0.2 × CP

⇒ Percentage Loss = (0.2 × CP ÷ CP) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is Loss 20%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cost Price & Selling Price

Profit occurs when Selling Price > Cost Price (Profit = SP − CP). Loss occurs when Cost Price > Selling Price (Loss = CP − SP).

Profit and Loss Percentage

Both profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price unless stated otherwise. Formula: Profit/Loss % = (Profit or Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Fractional Equivalents

Converting percentages to fractions speeds up calculations. For example, 33⅓% = 1/3, 20% = 1/5, and 40% = 2/5.
